title: Auth Calcification Audit — canonical structured output
description: The model of an audit run. Both markdown artifacts are rendered FROM this file: they may explain and synthesize beyond it, but may not state any claim (finding, status, anchor, count, ranking) that is not in it, and the renderer never re-reads the audited codebase. Every fact appears exactly once — counts are computed from arrays, ranking is array order, 'split' verdicts are derived by comparing per-vendor entries. Nothing in this schema names a specific vendor; vendor identity is data. Escape hatches: 'other' = pattern determined and understood but not in the current vocabulary (empirical taxonomies only; requires a note and at least one cited presence finding — harness-enforced); 'undetermined' = could not be determined (any detected verdict; requires a note and a paired coverage.gaps entry — harness-enforced). Never round an unknown to the nearest determined value.

scope.description: Repo or directory audited, as shown in the report title.

skill_version.description: From the `version` field in SKILL.md's frontmatter (kept in sync with plugin.json by a harness lint) — makes every output traceable to the skill version that produced it.

model_self_reported.description: Phase 0 self-report, verbatim. Imperfect by design; the human verifies.

disclaimer_fired.description: Whether the Phase 0 disclaimer condition triggered. Stored (not derived) because the condition includes 'uncertain about the model', which the JSON cannot capture; the harness asserts consistency with model_self_reported where it can.

id.description: Slug used as the key in boundary, axes.per_vendor, and findings.

detected.description: Human-readable name + version as detected (e.g. from package.json).

sdk_version.description: Version-qualified detection where the profile distinguishes versions (a finding stated without version qualification is incomplete — playbook). Omit only if genuinely undeterminable.

profile.description: Profile filename loaded from vendors/, or null for detected-but-unprofiled. INVARIANT (harness): profile == null ⇒ this vendor appears in coverage.gaps and in NO boundary or axis assessment — a gap, never a silent drop.

profile_verified.description: The profile's own verification date — the report metadata cites it, so the renderer needs it here (fresh-eyes rule). Include whenever profile is non-null.

coverage.description: What 'no finding' means depends entirely on this section. A clean-looking axis is only honest next to a populated coverage record.

reason.description: Why this was read in full (boundary module, config file, profile names it load-bearing…).

path.description: Path or glob swept via grep + confirm. Counts from here are confirmed hits, not exhaustive reads — the renderer must qualify them accordingly.

reason.description: Unparseable file, dynamic import, generated code, vendor without a profile, verdict recorded as 'undetermined'…

vendor.description: Set when the gap concerns a specific vendor (e.g. unprofiled vendor, undetermined verdict on that vendor's surface).

findings.description: THE canonical finding set — one flat array. Boundary signals, axes, backlog, and the headline all reference findings by id; a finding is never duplicated into the structures that cite it.

boundary.description: Keyed by vendor id — never a single collapsed verdict. A mid-migration codebase reads 'vendorA: present / vendorB: absent'; 'split' is derived by comparing entries, never stored. Every profiled vendor must have an entry (harness).

interview.description: Null when Phase 2 did not run (non-interactive, no answers file). The human's RAW input, preserved verbatim so the likelihood mapping below is auditable — what they said is a different fact from what the skill concluded.

source.description: 'live' = AskUserQuestion in-session; 'file' = pre-filled answers file. The renderer must note when answers came from a file, not a live maintainer.

judgment_calls.description: The questions the audit deliberately did not answer. INVARIANT (harness): every axis whose likelihood is null appears here (in non-interactive mode, all four interview questions route here per SKILL.md); non-axis questions (unprofiled vendors, migration intent, true retrofit cost) use axis: null.

context.description: Why this matters / what hinges on the answer.

backlog.description: Null when ranking was not performed (no human likelihood input) — null means 'not produced', an empty array would mean 'ranked, nothing to recommend'. Array ORDER is the ranking; there is no rank field, so a stored rank can never disagree with position.

task.description: Introduce the boundary / write the adapter / add the contract suite / own refresh / localize claims / move to access tokens…

why.description: Traceable to mechanical evidence × the maintainer's stated input. Qualitative cost only — NEVER a duration.

migration_readiness.description: Findings read forward, only for changes the maintainer flagged. Null when no change was flagged (always null in non-interactive runs).

change.description: The change the maintainer flagged, in their terms.

remaining.description: The specific missing pieces (contract suite, policy layer, N call sites…).

synthesis.description: The judgment layer. Written as prose in the markdown, but RECORDED here so (a) the agreement check can verify the rendered headline cites exactly these findings, and (b) a future judge layer can evaluate 'synthesis, not inventory' against a stable field.

posture.description: One-phrase structural verdict, e.g. 'mid-migration, split per vendor'.

text.description: The single most consequential finding or, preferably, a synthesis — mechanical fact × maintainer roadmap = named tension.

repoPath.description: Relative to the audited root — the same root the markdown links resolve against.

quote.description: EXACT text copied from the cited line(s) — never paraphrased, never reconstructed from memory. The harness re-reads file:line and asserts this text appears there; a mismatch is a fabricated or mis-anchored finding.

vendor.description: Null only for vendor-independent structural findings (e.g. no SSR surface exists, app code branches on execution context).

signals.description: Every boundary signal / axis this finding evidences — one leaked vendor type can serve both b1_anti_corruption and identity_provider. INVARIANT (harness): every assessment citing this finding must appear in this list, and vice versa.

statement.description: The one-line claim, plain language. Claim register only — explanation belongs in the rendered markdown, not here.

oneOf.description: PRESENCE claim — something exists at one or more locations. Mechanically verifiable via every evidence anchor's quote.

evidence.description: One finding, possibly several anchors (e.g. an import line + the call line that together constitute the pattern).

oneOf.description: ABSENCE claim — searched and not found. Unquotable by nature, so it carries its search record instead. INVARIANT (harness): checked_patterns must cover every alternative pattern the loaded profile lists for this concern — the playbook's 'negative findings demand a second look', made assertable.

status.description: 'not_applicable' = the concern does not arise in this codebase (e.g. no SSR surface) — a DETERMINED fact, ideally backed by an absence finding. 'undetermined' = could not assess (unparseable, dynamic, out of reach) — must pair with a coverage.gaps entry (harness); never round to 'absent', that is the false all-clear.

finding_ids.description: Every determined verdict (present/partial/absent) is evidence-backed — at least one finding, whether presence or absence. May be empty only for not_applicable/undetermined.

note.description: The key gap or nuance, e.g. 'present but no contract suite'.

likelihood.description: The skill's NORMALIZED reading of the maintainer's answer ('Yes — planned' → high; 'No — locked in' → none). Null when unanswered. INVARIANT (harness): non-null ⇔ interview.answers has this axis, and the mapping matches the documented table. Never inferred from code.

costEvidence.description: The skill's MECHANICAL cost read — present in every run, human or not. Distinct from the maintainer's true retrofit cost, which is theirs to state.

basis.description: Concrete mechanical justification: boundary quality, spread of coupling, confirmed call-site counts. NEVER a duration — no hours, days, weeks, sprints.

answer.description: The chosen option label verbatim (or free text). The human's words, not a normalization.

notes.description: Anything else they said ('RBAC in Q3').

classification.description: builtin_selector = a built-in persistence selector passed to the storage seam. It is NOT a custom adapter — classifying it as one is the look-alike trap (a serious accuracy error). vendor_default = nothing configured. 'other' = understood pattern outside this vocabulary (note + ≥1 presence finding required). 'undetermined' = could not determine (note + coverage.gaps entry required).

recommended_seam.description: The bounded shape from the methodology, in prose.

cost_confirmed.description: The maintainer's own cost confirmation when supplied (answers file). The skill NEVER fills this itself.

classification.description: 'partial' = owned shape with gaps (no single-flight, no failure path) or ownership split across surfaces (server owned, client inherited) — the gaps themselves are separate findings. 'other'/'undetermined' per the escape-hatch rules (top-level description).
Is provider-specific feature usage confined to the adapter, or spread across app code? 'other'/'undetermined' per the escape-hatch rules.

claims_handling.description: 'principal_without_policy' = vendor claims are mapped to a domain Principal, but app code still reads Principal fields directly — a present boundary with a gap. 'other'/'undetermined' per the escape-hatch rules.

api_token_type.description: What populates the outbound Authorization header. 'opaque' = a token the profile identifies as non-JWT/invalid for API auth (a determined fact, not an unknown). 'not_applicable' = no outbound API auth exists. 'undetermined' = could not determine — coverage.gaps pairing required.
